name: clawmetry-setup-openclaw
description: Pinned OpenClaw CLI for the setup-openclaw composite action. CI-only: nothing here ships in the clawmetry wheel or is imported by the dashboard.
//overrides: The openclaw pin is 2026.9.2. At the pins recorded below `npm audit` reports
0 advisories. Re-run it rather than believing this line: the paragraph below
is about exactly how this sentence went stale once before.
WHAT THIS CORRECTS (2026-11-13). The previous revision of this note said 'the
tree is advisory-clean, npm audit reports 0 vulnerabilities', and by
2026-11-13 that had quietly stopped being true. Nothing in this directory had
changed. New advisories had simply been published against the exact versions
these overrides pin, and an exact-version override freezes the tree against
exactly that drift. Measured on this branch:
before  12 advisories / 5 high / 0 critical
after    2 advisories / 0 high / 0 critical
WHAT THIS ADDS (2026-11-14). The 2 moderates that measurement left behind are
now 0. Measured on this branch, same flags:
before   2 advisories / 0 high / 0 critical
after    0 advisories
The whole of that difference is the one bare `minimatch` key. Why 11.0.5 and
not 11.0.8, the latest: .github/dependabot.yml holds every ecosystem in this
repository to a 7-day cooldown, on the reasoning that a release adopted the
hour it is published is adopted inside the window a compromised version is
published into. 11.0.6, 11.0.7 and 11.0.8 were all published within 4 days of
this measurement; 11.0.5 (2026-11-05) is the newest release that is both past
that cooldown and at or above the 11.0.1 the advisory is fixed in. A pin
chosen this way is a floor, not a ceiling -- Dependabot moves it once the
newer releases age past the same window.
No Node move: minimatch 11.0.5 declares `engines.node 20 || >=22`, which
drops 18 from what 10.2.6 allowed. All seven workflows that use this action
take its bare `22` default and none passes a node-version of its own, so
nothing in the fleet is on a major this excludes -- checked, not assumed.
Behaviour was compared rather than assumed, because minimatch 11 is a rewrite
of the matching engine and this tree uses it for globbing: 837 (pattern, file)
pairs over 27 patterns -- globstars, extglobs, brace expansion, negation,
character classes, escapes -- evaluated under both 10.2.6 and 11.0.5, with 0
differences. The public export surface is also unchanged (minimatch, sep,
GLOBSTAR, filter, defaults, braceExpand, match, Minimatch, escape, unescape).
The five highs were @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, body-parser, undici, zod, and
openclaw's own roll-up of those. Every one had a fix inside the major this
tree already resolves, so the fix was to move the pins, not the openclaw
version. Each pin below was re-measured rather than bumped to 'latest'.
THE FIRST LESSON. An exact-version override is a dated measurement, not a
standing guarantee. It does not drift forward when a patch lands and it does
not warn you. So treat a clean `npm audit` quoted in this file as evidence
about the day it was run, and re-run it rather than reading this note and
believing it. That is how five highs sat here unnoticed.

The three inert keys stay for the reason they always have: each is a no-op
while its package is absent and each becomes correct again the moment a
future openclaw pulls that package back in. Delete them only with a fresh
audit in hand.
Keys stay range-scoped (name@major) for the original reason: a bare `undici`
key would also rewrite any undici@7 a transitive resolves, which is a major
bump for that consumer. Two keys are bare. `basic-ftp` is the older one and
the reason it is safe is recorded with its 2026-10-01 measurement in git
history; it is inert now anyway. `minimatch` is bare for a different and
stronger reason, recorded 2026-11-14: the collateral a range-scope exists to
prevent has no instance here. The lockfile holds exactly ONE minimatch node
(node_modules/minimatch), and exactly one package requests it -- openclaw, at
the exact version 10.2.6. There is no second consumer on another major for a
bare key to rewrite. Check that again before widening any other key.
THE SECOND LESSON, learned the hard way on 2026-11-13: VERIFY WITH `npm ci`,
NOT `npm install`. A cross-major override key was tried then --
`minimatch@10` resolving to 11.0.8 -- to clear the two moderates. It
took the tree to 0 advisories and `npm install` accepted it without a
murmur. `npm ci`, which is what this action actually runs, then refused the
lockfile it had just written:
npm error `npm ci` can only install packages when your package.json and
npm error package-lock.json [...] are in sync.
npm error Missing: minimatch@10.2.6 from lock file
So that key was dropped, and the note recorded the moderate as unfixable. It
was the KEY FORM that was wrong, not the fix: a range-scoped `minimatch@10`
leaves package.json asking for a 10.x the lockfile no longer contains, which
is precisely what `npm ci` compares. A bare key resolves the edge
unconditionally, so the two stay in sync -- verified 2026-11-14 by `npm ci`
from a deleted node_modules, twice. The cost of not catching the first attempt
would have been every caller of this action failing at install, which is the
whole E2E fleet. A clean `npm install` plus a clean `npm audit` is not
evidence that this directory works; `npm ci` from a deleted node_modules is.
RUN THE BOOT GATE TOO, FOR ANY CHANGE TO THIS FILE OR THE LOCKFILE. This is
the older lesson and it still holds. `npm ci` succeeds and `openclaw
--version` prints a version even when the module graph is broken: neither
loads the graph. The gate that catches it is booting the gateway, which is
what .github/workflows/openclaw-boot.yml does:
openclaw gateway --port 18789 --verbose --allow-unconfigured
# then poll http://127.0.0.1:18789/ for any HTTP response
It reproduces locally in about five seconds and logs 'http server listening'
then 'ready' when the tree is sound. Run it, not just --version.
Boot gate run for THIS change (bare `minimatch` -> 11.0.5), on Node 22.23.4:
HTTP 200 on the first poll, 'http server listening (13 plugins: anthropic,
browser, canvas, cua-computer, device-pair, file-transfer, geolocation,
linux-node, memory-core, ollama, openai, talk-voice, xai; 3.6s)', on OpenClaw
2026.9.2 (3928bad) -- the same 13 plugins and the same commit the previous
revision recorded, so replacing the glob engine does not disturb the module
graph. `npm ci` from a deleted node_modules was run twice and installed 333
packages both times. That is 332 before plus exactly one: minimatch 11 adds
@isaacs/nonrecursive-glob-match (1.1.0), which is the rewrite the fix is.
THE TWO MODERATES, CLEARED 2026-11-14. The previous revision of this note
recorded these as having no fix this tree could take. That was true of the
key form tried at the time, not of the tree:
minimatch  GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249, globparts amplification, range >=7.0.0
<11.0.1. Cleared by the bare `minimatch` key above. There is no
fix inside 10.x, so this needs a cross-major key -- but a BARE
one, not the range-scoped `minimatch@10` that `npm ci` rejected.
npm's own offered alternative remains an openclaw downgrade of
several months, which is not taken.
openclaw   The roll-up of the minimatch finding, not a separate defect. It
cleared with it.
WHY THE OPENCLAW PIN DOES NOT MOVE HERE. `npm audit` offers a newer openclaw
as the fix for the highs cleared above and for the minimatch moderate. That
is a real option and it is deliberately not taken, because the newer releases
raise engines.node past this action's bare `22` default and moving that moves
every caller -- ci.yml (live-openclaw-e2e), e2e-nightly.yml,
moat-keystone-drive-nightly.yml, openclaw-boot.yml, oss-golden-path.yml and
pr-screenshots.yml, all six of which take the default. A Node major for the
E2E fleet is a decision with an owner; clearing published advisories in CI
tooling is not. The pins above clear every advisory without touching Node, so
that decision stays open rather than being forced by an advisory.
THE MIRROR IN clawmetry-cloud. vivekchand/clawmetry-cloud carries a copy of
this action pinning the same openclaw 2026.9.2 with NO overrides block, and
it refreshed its lockfile on 2026-11-13. Measured the same day, that copy
reports 5 advisories / 4 high -- the same mcp-sdk, undici, zod and openclaw
roll-up this block now clears. The two copies share a mechanism rather than a
release cadence, so this is reported there rather than cross-pushed; the fix
there is an overrides block like this one, not another lockfile refresh,
because a refresh is what it already did.
